findings.title: Notification preferences are stored and displayed but never enforced on any send path
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/api/src/lib/notification-channels.ts:56-113 resolves notification_preferences (module + global 'all' rows, exact org when known, default-on fail-safe, sms excluded at :43-44) and both senders consult it: api/lib/notify.ts:307-312 and worker/tasks/scheduled-notifications.ts:228-230,341-345,428-431. Tests notification-channels.test.ts + notify-enforcement.test.ts.

findings.title: API-originated notifications bypass the dedup unique index
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the code path is correct (notify.ts:100-123 and worker notification-store.ts:167-180 upsert ON CONFLICT (notification_key)) and migration 5302463_fix_notification_key_dedup_index.sql:36-39 replaces the 5302107 partial index with a full unique index; the migration header records 536 42P10 failures on dev, so the 7dd0402 'verified-fixed' claim was premature. Residual: 5302463 is also the version of 5302463_client_portal_ai_and_visibility.sql; scripts/preflight-check.sh:50-51 fails on the duplicate and `supabase db push` keys by version (.github/workflows/supabase-migrations.yml:71-90), so the dedup fix can be skipped on a fresh environment (tracked as INV-P1-001/DATA-P1-004). The new notification-dedup-index.test.ts checks the index chain, not apply order.

findings.title: No delivery observability: email/notification failures are silent and unalerted
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: alert rules MCTNotificationDeliveryFailureRateHigh and MCTNotificationEmailSkipped in infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:262-304 (26 rules validate with promtool); terminal-outcome counters in api/lib/metrics.ts:246-253 and worker/metrics.ts; SLO #4 documented in docs/SLO.md:20-27.

findings.title: Notification preference writes from the web UI omit organization_id (NOT NULL) so toggles cannot persist
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/api/src/routes/notification-preferences.ts:52-70 defaults organizationId to req.orgId/req.query and 400s when unresolvable; the UI surfaces save failures and refetches (NotificationPreferencesClient.tsx:112-125).

findings.title: Web Push channel is entirely absent (no subscriptions, no VAPID, no service worker)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: table+RLS+enum in supabase/migrations/5302453_push_subscriptions.sql; API routes/push-subscriptions.ts (VAPID public key, owner-scoped upsert/soft revoke); worker RFC 8291/8292 sender apps/worker/src/push.ts + tasks/notification-push.ts (404/410 revoke); SW push/notificationclick handlers apps/web/public/sw.js; UI PushNotificationSettings.tsx + lib/push.ts; API enqueue path notify.ts:232-290 with idempotency claim.

findings.title: SMTP remains optional; email silently degrades to no-op in production
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the silence is fixed (api/main.ts:24-33 logs an error naming missing SMTP_* keys; worker/env.ts:103-104 warns; email.ts:24-28 + worker/email.ts:16-19 meter skipped; MCTNotificationEmailSkipped alerts). Remaining unchanged: SMTP is still optional and the deploy does not gate on it (deploy-do.yml:671-674 forwards SMTP_* but never fails when unset) - email stays a no-op until the operator provisions it.

findings.title: Worker lacks an `unhandledRejection` handler
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/worker/src/main.ts:35-47 handles uncaughtException and unhandledRejection; the API also handles both at apps/api/src/main.ts:94-99.

findings.title: Scheduled reminder inserts and email sends are not atomic; retries can double-send
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: claimNotificationEmail uses the notification_key upsert as the atomic email claim with an idempotency-store fallback (worker notification-store.ts:212-226; scheduled-notifications.ts:267,383,468) and the API mirrors it (notify.ts:189-201).

findings.title: Sensitive ticket content is stored and emailed verbatim with no sensitivity filter
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: redactSensitiveContent is applied before storage and email in both deployables (api/lib/notification-content.ts:78, notify.ts:73-79,455; worker/notification-content.ts:74, scheduled-notifications.ts:213-214,351-352,436-437); it covers credential assignments, bearer tokens, PEM blocks, provider token shapes, SSN and Luhn-valid cards.

findings.title: API inline email fallback has no retry and ignores the send result
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/api/src/lib/email.ts:14-63 retries 3x with linear backoff and returns a boolean; callers record the terminal outcome.

findings.title: Realtime/SSE notification channel is scoped by user only, with no org assertion
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:181-192 drops SSE rows whose organization_id does not match the resolved org; the initial query applies the same predicate (:303). mark-all-read is user_id-scoped and optionally org-filtered (:419-433), so it cannot touch another user's rows; the admin create endpoint asserts the recipient shares the active org (:459-460). Regression test notifications-org-scope.test.ts.

findings.title: Backup-failure alerting is present but cannot be trusted to deliver
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: db-backup.yml:134-140 and storage-backup.yml:112-118 fail the step with ::error when neither ntfy nor Slack delivery succeeds, so a swallowed notification cannot pass as success.

findings.title: notifyAndEmail enqueues email even when the in-app notification was deduped
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: notifyAndEmail skips the email when inApp.deduped and falls back to the idempotency-store claim when the in-app channel was preference-suppressed (notify.ts:192-199 claim, :395-401 skip).

findings.title: Notification delivery SLO counts a queued email hand-off as success and excludes worker send outcomes
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the API records a successful enqueue as status=queued (api/lib/metrics.ts:246-253) and SLO #4 + the failure-ratio alert compute from worker terminal outcomes only (docs/SLO.md:20-27; prometheus.rules.yml:262-290).

findings.title: Alertmanager→ntfy critical alert delivery is optional in production and has no in-repo exercise evidence
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the off-box Watchdog URL still fails prod deploys (deploy-do.yml:845-863) and the renderer/receivers are wired (infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml:78-152). Remaining unchanged: a missing ALERTMANAGER_CRITICAL_WEBHOOK_URL or relay credentials only warns (deploy-do.yml:865-868), and docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:391 still records delivery as not exercised end-to-end (OBS-P2-014) - no in-repo artifact proves a critical alert reached ntfy.

findings.title: No email template system; repetitive inline HTML diverges between senders
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: shared packages/sdk/src/email-template.ts (renderEmailLayout/buildNotificationEmail/footer links, escaping) is used by the API (notify.ts:12-17,424-468) and the worker (scheduled-notifications.ts:16,68-82).

findings.title: `sms` channel is a dead preference option; UI copy misstates enforcement
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: both preference UIs offer email/in_app/push only (NotificationPreferencesClient.tsx:19-23; NotificationBell.tsx:205,267) and the resolver documents sms as non-deliverable and excludes it (notification-channels.ts:16,43-44). The API enum still accepts the legacy sms value, which is inert.

findings.title: SSE polling fallback interval is not cleared on unmount
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:40,96-104 stores the fallback interval in a ref and clears it on cleanup.

findings.title: `notification-preferences` PUT accepts a body `organizationId` without `assertOrgScopeMatches`
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: requireOrgAccess (mounted at notification-preferences.ts:9-10) resolves and validates req.body.organizationId via extractOrgId (middleware/org-access.ts:9-12) before the handler runs; the handler prefers req.orgId (notification-preferences.ts:62-64).

findings.title: No unsubscribe link or global opt-out in notification emails
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: HMAC-signed unsubscribe links are embedded in every org-scoped email (api/lib/unsubscribe-token.ts; notify.ts:432-441; worker scheduled-notifications.ts:16,68-82) and the public endpoint writes a module_key='all' opt-out honoured by both resolvers (routes/notification-unsubscribe.ts:24-43,127; notification-channels.ts:64-68).

findings.title: Worker reminder preference lookups omit the organization, so any org's opt-out suppresses the channel for all
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: every resolveChannels call in the worker passes the notification's organization (scheduled-notifications.ts:228-230,341-345,428-431) and the resolver filters by org when known (notification-channels.ts:70-78).

findings.title: No per-recipient send throttle on notification producers
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: apps/api/src/lib/notification-throttle.ts:20-32 (30/hour per hashed recipient, Redis INCR with per-process fallback, fail-open) is applied in notifyAndEmail (notify.ts:404-420) and the worker (scheduled-notifications.ts:52-56) with a throttled metric.

findings.title: Worker ticket-responded email builds the deep link from unescaped payload metadata (latent XSS-in-email)
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5: the ticket id is percent-encoded before becoming a path segment (scheduled-notifications.ts:392) and the shared template escapes body and URL (packages/sdk/src/email-template.ts:18,48-55).

findings.title: One-click unsubscribe is an unauthenticated GET with no expiry or confirmation; mail-security link scanners can silently opt users out
findings.note: re-verified at 6b7aa1a5, now closed: GET renders a confirmation page and performs no write (routes/notification-unsubscribe.ts:110-125); POST performs the opt-out (:127-155); the token carries a mandatory 90-day exp (lib/unsubscribe-token.ts:33,72-78; worker mirror :20,71); RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe/-Post headers are built (:84-90) and forwarded through api/lib/email.ts:11-14,47-50 and worker/email.ts:10-13,44-47; CSRF is skipped only for this route (middleware/csrf.ts:68-73); tests notification-unsubscribe.test.ts + unsubscribe-token.test.ts.

findings.title: Global email opt-out is invisible and cannot be reversed in the notification-preferences UI
findings.note: NEW at 6b7aa1a5: the one-click unsubscribe writes notification_preferences{module_key:'all', channel:'email', enabled:false} (routes/notification-unsubscribe.ts:127-134) and resolveChannels suppresses email whenever any matching row is false (lib/notification-channels.ts:64-88). But the preferences API only accepts moduleKey in tickets/projects/documents/billing/system (routes/notification-preferences.ts:13,51) and both UIs render only those modules and look up per-module rows (NotificationPreferencesClient.tsx:14-23,70-71,94-100; NotificationBell.tsx:205,267). After unsubscribing there is no per-module row, so every email toggle continues to display ON; saving cannot clear the 'all' row and there is no DELETE/resubscribe endpoint. The user cannot restore email notifications without operator action. Fix: expose the global opt-out as its own toggle and allow PUT moduleKey='all' (or delete the row).

findings.title: One-click unsubscribe changes delivery preferences without an audit event
findings.note: NEW at 6b7aa1a5: POST /notifications/unsubscribe writes notification_preferences through the service-role client (routes/notification-unsubscribe.ts:122-141) and only logs to the application logger (:143-147); there is no logAuditEvent call and no audit row, whereas the authenticated PUT records action 'notification_preference.update' (routes/notification-preferences.ts:94-101). A security-relevant change to a user's delivery preferences - including a leaked-link or forged opt-out - therefore has no audit trail for incident review or DSAR reconstruction. Add a system-actor audit event (userId, organizationId, surface=unsubscribe) without the raw token.

report: Read-only re-verification at 6b7aa1a5. 21/24 previous NOTIF findings are verified fixed, 3 are partially fixed (NOTIF-P1-002, NOTIF-P2-002, NOTIF-P2-011), 0 regressed. NOTIF-P2-012 (prefetching scanners silently opting users out) is closed: GET is side-effect free, POST performs RFC 8058 one-click, tokens expire after 90 days and List-Unsubscribe/-Post headers are sent. NOTIF-P1-002 remains partial only because the fix migration shares version 5302463 with another migration, so `supabase db push` can skip it (preflight fails; see INV-P1-001); the 42P10 bug it fixes was real (536 dev failures) and the 7dd0402 claim was premature. SMTP provisioning and critical-alert delivery remain operator-gated (P2-002/P2-011). Two new findings: NOTIF-P2-013 (global unsubscribe is invisible/irreversible in the UI) and NOTIF-P3-009 (unsubscribe writes no audit row). Executed: promtool check rules (26 SUCCESS) + rule tests (SUCCESS); read all notification senders, push path, SSE scoping and unsubscribe tests. Residual outside NOTIF: alert delivery remains unexercised (OBS-P2-014) and the unsubscribe URL still carries a reusable bearer token in the query string (browser history/Referer), accepted for one-click compatibility.
